citeAs: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (2023). CommonCanvas: An Open Diffusion Model Trained with Creative-Commons Images. arXiv:2310.16825.
creator: Aaron Gokaslan, A. Feder Cooper, Jasmine Collins, Landan Seguin, Austin Jacobson, Mihir Patel, Jonathan Frankle, Cory Stephenson, Volodymyr Kuleshov (Cornell Tech, Databricks Mosaic)
description: CommonCatalog-C is a dataset of approximately 26 million Creative-Commons-licensed images sourced from YFCC100M (via Flickr), restricted to images licensed for commercial use (CC-BY and CC-BY-SA licenses). Each image is paired with a high-quality synthetic caption generated by a pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. It is a subset of the larger CommonCatalog-NC dataset and was curated to train open text-to-image diffusion models without relying on web-scraped data of unclear copyright provenance.
name: CommonCatalog-C
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: BLIP-2-generated captions were found to be qualitatively more descriptive than corresponding LAION-2B ground-truth alt-text captions. Quantitatively, BLIP-2 captions achieve higher CLIP Scores than ground-truth captions (corroborated by Nguyen et al.), but at the cost of reduced caption diversity as measured by unique trigrams. Approximately 30.76% of CommonCatalog-C images had existing alt-text captions.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Synthetic captions were generated for all images using the pre-trained BLIP-2 OPT2.5B model. BLIP-2 was selected based on qualitative analysis and its state-of-the-art performance on MS COCO. The captioning process required approximately 1,120 GPU A100 hours. Images were center-cropped and resized to 512x512 pixels before captioning. Approximately 30.76% of CommonCatalog-C images had existing alt-text captions.
rai:dataBiases: The YFCC100M source data is approximately a decade old, meaning CC images are not as current as those in LAION-2B. The dataset underperforms in categories such as faces, general photography, and paintings compared to LAION-trained models. Synthetic captions generated by BLIP-2 exhibit reduced diversity of n-grams compared to ground-truth captions. BLIP-2 captions are higher quality than ground-truth alt-text but at the cost of caption diversity. The dataset's domain differs from web-scraped conceptual captions, causing domain shift on certain benchmarks.
rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the YFCC100M dataset by re-scraping high-resolution images from Flickr using the Flickr IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. Only images with Creative-Commons licenses that allow derivative works were retained. CommonCatalog-C specifically includes only images licensed for commercial use (CC-BY 2.0 and CC-BY-SA 2.0), yielding approximately 26 million images (26,232,417). Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw source data is the YFCC100M dataset, which consists of 100 million Creative-Commons-licensed images and multimedia files from Flickr. The images were re-scraped at very high resolution (exceeding 4K) from Flickr using the Flickr IDs provided in the YFCC100M metadata. The original YFCC100M images were low-resolution and thus not directly used.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains roughly 70 million CC images total (26 million for the commercial subset), which is less than 3% the size of LAION-2B. The YFCC100M source data is about a decade old, so images are not as current as LAION-2B. Synthetic captions have reduced n-gram diversity compared to human-written captions. Models trained on this data underperform in categories like faces, general photography, and paintings. Although CC images are used, adversarial prompts can still produce content resembling iconic characters.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For caption generation, images were center-cropped and resized to a maximum size of 512x512 pixels before being passed to BLIP-2. At training time of the diffusion model, all images remain in their native resolution. Images with non-derivative (ND) licenses were excluded. Images were further filtered by license type: CommonCatalog-C retains only CC-BY 2.0 and CC-BY-SA 2.0 licensed images.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to address copyright concerns in training generative AI models by using only openly licensed Creative-Commons images with known provenance. It provides a reproducible alternative to LAION-based datasets, which suffer from link rot and unclear copyright status. The paper demonstrates that models trained on this dataset are less likely to generate recognizable copyrighted characters (e.g., Disney characters, Snoopy) compared to SD2 trained on LAION.
rai:dataUseCases: Training text-to-image generative diffusion models on openly licensed data. The dataset is intended as an alternative to web-scraped datasets like LAION-2B for training high-quality T2I models while avoiding copyright concerns. CommonCatalog-C specifically supports commercial use cases.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: BLIP-2 OPT2.5B (pre-trained image-to-text model) was used to generate synthetic captions for all CC images. BLIP-2 consists of a frozen visual encoder, a learned transformer network, and a frozen large language model (LLM). It was pre-trained on LAION-400M.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains images of people, including public figures and celebrities, sourced from Flickr via YFCC100M. The paper notes that models trained on the dataset can generate some noteworthy public figures (e.g., Barack Obama, Elon Musk, Kim Kardashian), though less accurately than SD2.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each image receives one synthetic caption from BLIP-2; no multiple independent annotations per item are described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotations are machine-generated by BLIP-2; no human annotators are used for the dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform used; captions are generated automatically by BLIP-2 model.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper does not explicitly discuss missing data handling in the collection process.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol described; missing captions are handled by generating synthetic ones via BLIP-2, which is covered under annotation protocol.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, balancing, resampling) is described for the dataset itself; training augmentations are model training details, not dataset properties.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described for the dataset.
